steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http, url, and querystring modules using require() statements at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. Separate each import with a comma or place them on separate lines.
steps.seedCode: // Import http, url, and querystring modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: Your file will have the three required modules imported and ready to use for profiling.
successCriteria: The http, url, and querystring modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Node.js modules needed for profiling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import all three modules: http, url, and querystring.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: use require('module_name') for each import. Make sure you're importing http, url, and querystring.

steps.title: Create the main server function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'createServer' that initializes an HTTP server and listens on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use the http.createServer() method and call server.listen() with port 3000 and a console log message.
steps.seedCode:
// Import http, url, and querystring modules here

// Create the main server function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createServer that sets up an HTTP server listening on port 3000.
successCriteria: The createServer function is defined, uses http.createServer(), and calls server.listen(3000) with a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the server function that will listen for incoming requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named 'createServer' and includes both http.createServer() and server.listen(3000) with a console log.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server function isn't set up correctly. Check that you're using http.createServer() and calling listen() on port 3000.

steps.title: Initialize slow query tracking object
steps.instruction: Inside your server function, create an empty object named 'slowQueries' to store slow query information.
steps.hint: Declare a variable using 'const' or 'let' and assign it an empty object {}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty tracking object
const userSessions = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: The server function now contains a 'slowQueries' object that will be used to track query timing data.
successCriteria: An empty object named 'slowQueries' is declared inside the server function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the data structure that will track slow queries.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared an empty object named 'slowQueries' inside the server function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'slowQueries' object is missing or incorrectly placed. It should be an empty object declared inside the server function.

steps.title: Initialize slow route tracking array
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, create an empty array named 'slowRoutes' to store slow route information.
steps.hint: You can declare an array using const and square brackets: const slowRoutes = [];
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty array
const items = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The server function will have a 'slowRoutes' array variable ready to store route paths and response times.
successCriteria: An empty array named 'slowRoutes' is declared inside the server function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the slow route tracking array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared an array named 'slowRoutes' inside the server function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slow route tracking array wasn't created correctly. Try declaring 'const slowRoutes = [];' inside the server function.

steps.title: Create query parsing helper function
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, create a helper function named parseQuery that takes a URL string as a parameter and returns parsed query parameters using the querystring module.
steps.hint: You can use querystring.parse() after extracting the query string from the URL. Remember to extract the query portion after the '?' character.
steps.expectedOutcome: A parseQuery function is defined inside the server function that can extract and parse query parameters from URLs.
successCriteria: The parseQuery function is created, takes a URL parameter, extracts the query string, and uses querystring.parse() to return parsed parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the parseQuery helper function. This will be essential for analyzing query parameters in incoming requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your parseQuery function takes a URL parameter, extracts the query string (the part after '?'), and uses querystring.parse() to return the parsed object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parseQuery function isn't quite right. It should extract the query string from the URL and parse it using querystring.parse(). Check the analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Create slow query detection hook
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, create a function named detectSlowQuery that takes queryString and startTime as parameters.
steps.hint: Define the function with the given name and parameters. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A detectSlowQuery function is defined inside the server function with the correct parameters.
successCriteria: The detectSlowQuery function exists with queryString and startTime parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the slow query detection hook function with the proper parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but check the name or parameters. It should be named detectSlowQuery and accept queryString and startTime.
steps.feedbackWrong: The detectSlowQuery function is not properly defined. Make sure to create it inside the server function with the specified parameters.

steps.title: Create slow route detection hook
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, create a function named detectSlowRoute that takes startTime and routePath as parameters, calculates the elapsed time, and adds the route to the slowRoutes array if it exceeds 2000ms.
steps.hint: You can calculate elapsed time with Date.now() - startTime. Use an if statement to check if it's greater than 2000, then push an object with route and duration to slowRoutes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A detectSlowRoute function is added inside the server function that monitors route response time and conditionally adds slow routes to the tracking array.
successCriteria: The detectSlowRoute function is defined with startTime and routePath parameters, calculates elapsed time, checks if it exceeds 2000ms, and pushes an object with route and duration to slowRoutes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the slow route detection hook. This function will help identify routes that take too long to respond.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it calculates elapsed time correctly and conditionally adds to slowRoutes when exceeding 2000ms.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that you're calculating elapsed time with Date.now() - startTime and pushing to slowRoutes only when it exceeds 2000ms.

steps.title: Implement request handling with profiling hooks
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, after the helper functions, add code to call both profiling hooks for each incoming request. Start by calling the slow query detection hook with the parsed query object, then call the slow route detection hook with the request URL.
steps.hint: You'll need to parse the query from the request URL first, then pass it to the slow query detection hook. Then pass the request URL to the slow route detection hook.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server function now includes calls to both profiling hooks that will execute for every incoming request.
successCriteria: Both profiling hooks are called inside the server function with appropriate parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully integrated the profiling hooks into the request handling pipeline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but make sure both hooks are called with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The profiling hooks aren't properly integrated. Remember to call both hooks inside the server function.

steps.title: Add profiling data endpoint
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, add a route handler that returns the slowQueries object and slowRoutes array as JSON when the request URL path is '/profiling-data'.
steps.hint: Check if req.url starts with '/profiling-data', then set appropriate headers and send a JSON response using JSON.stringify.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will respond with JSON containing profiling data when accessing '/profiling-data'.
successCriteria: A route handler is added that checks for '/profiling-data' and returns slowQueries and slowRoutes as JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the profiling data endpoint that returns the tracking data as JSON.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to check the URL path and return both slowQueries and slowRoutes in the JSON response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint isn't working as expected. Check if you're correctly handling the '/profiling-data' route and returning JSON with both data structures.

steps.title: Test the profiler with sample requests
steps.instruction: Inside the server function, add a console.log statement at the end to output the slowQueries and slowRoutes data after processing requests.
steps.hint: Add console.log(slowQueries) and console.log(slowRoutes) before the closing brace of the server function to see the profiling data.
steps.analogousExample:
// Logging data after processing
console.log({ queries: slowQueries, routes: slowRoutes });
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will log the slowQueries object and slowRoutes array to the console after processing requests, allowing you to verify the profiler collects data.
successCriteria: The server function includes console.log statements for both slowQueries and slowRoutes at the end of its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the logging statements. Now when you run the server and make requests, you'll see the profiling data in the console.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some logging, but make sure to include both slowQueries and slowRoutes in the console.log statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server function doesn't have the required console.log statements for profiling data. Add them at the end of the function body.
